title: Supercharge Your Pitches with Storytelling
placement: After the comparison of competing emphasis.
watchFor: A story needs a clear problem and purpose. Apply that communication principle to deciding what the frame should convey.
useNext: Write one sentence describing the story of your café portrait, then identify an element that supports or competes with it.
captions: Original Stanford publisher transcript read. In-player caption availability is distinct from the transcript review.
reviewedEvidence: Read the full Stephanie Lampkin publisher transcript; reviewed the three-question structure and her personal storytelling context. Transcript: https://stvp.stanford.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2024/09/supercharge-your-pitches-with-storytelling-transcript.pdf
playbackStatus: Original YouTube player loaded and advanced for a short sample in an isolated browser on 2026-09-20. This verifies playback availability, not that the entire video was watched or the in-app embed works.
context: Acceptance-fixture reuse of a reviewed general storytelling clip; it is not photography instruction and is not evidence for camera behavior. The fixture deliberately uses the unverified-embed fallback and does not request a remote player.
limits: Founder-pitch advice adapted to demo narrative. Its general memory/brain assertion is not used as a scientific claim; narrative must not conceal limitations.

candidatesCompared.title: Mapping Customer Pains to Value Proposition
candidatesCompared.decision: Reviewed full original transcript and playback sample. Strong for evidence of value; selected Lampkin for its compact narrative structure before constructing a demo.

fallback.title: Choose the intended story
fallback.markdown: Name the person’s intended role in the photograph. Compare a frame that emphasizes expression with one that also explains the café setting. Keep the frame that serves the stated purpose.
